propositions: The reconciler unconditionally advances the cursor to the newest event in the fetched window, regardless of which candidates were successfully voted or which failed with retryable errors, causing abandoned candidates to fall outside all future event windows and never be re-driven.

A patch-set upload that triggers a review timeout or other retryable error on the reconciler's first pass is permanently dropped from future passes because the cursor moves past it, making the change invisible until a human posts a recheck-review comment or rebases.
The cursor is a server-side inclusive lower bound on event timestamps (`?t1=` parameter), so once advanced past an event, that event is unreachable in all subsequent reconcile windows.

The low-water mark must partition candidates into retryable holds (errors, deferred, timeouts) and terminal advances (voted, all skipped reasons) to avoid re-driving merged or abandoned changes into permanent failures.
Queue depth and held-back candidate tracking are not observable to operators, making it impossible to distinguish between a bot that is down, running, queued, or silently dropping a change.
